issue.standard_remedy: Route off-contract buying to contracted suppliers
issue.summary: 73% of category spend is off contract

plan.diagnosis: 73% of Hydraulic components category spend ($37,575,636 of $51,747,400 total spend) is occurring off-contract across 9 plants, representing high-severity maverick spend in a direct material category. The root cause is lack of contract enforcement and supplier compliance in a multi-ERP environment (SAP, Oracle EBS, Dynamics 365, NetSuite, Coupa) where users are procuring outside established agreements, likely due to inadequate system controls, missing preferred supplier catalogs, or plant-level purchasing autonomy bypassing contracts.

remedy_steps.step: Conduct urgent forensic analysis of all $37,575,636 maverick transactions across all 9 plants to identify top non-contracted suppliers, part numbers, and purchasing patterns by ERP system
Negotiate contract expansion or emergency blanket POs with existing contracted suppliers to cover the maverick part portfolio, targeting 90% coverage of the $37,575,636 spend with contracted pricing

Implement system-level procurement controls: enable approved vendor lists, create source lists for hydraulic components, and establish PO approval workflows for non-contracted spend >$5,000 in all five ERP systems
Deploy preferred supplier catalogs and punch-out connections to contracted hydraulic suppliers in Coupa and integrate with SAP, Oracle EBS, Dynamics 365, and NetSuite requisitioning modules
Execute plant-by-plant training program for all 9 facilities on mandatory contract compliance, new system controls, and escalation procedures for legitimate non-catalog requirements
Establish monthly maverick spend monitoring dashboard with plant-level KPIs and implement quarterly business reviews with contracted suppliers to assess coverage gaps and performance

plan.expected_impact: Reducing maverick spend from 73% to 15% of category spend will shift $30,000,000 to contracted suppliers, generating estimated savings of $2,250,000 to $3,750,000 annually (7.5-12.5% cost avoidance based on contract vs. spot pricing).
kpis: Maverick spend as % of Hydraulic components category spend (target: <15% within 6 months)
Contract compliance rate by plant (target: >85% per plant)
Number of active hydraulic suppliers (target: consolidate from current baseline by 30%)
Average price variance: contracted vs. maverick purchases (track monthly)
PO count through contracted catalogs vs. manual POs (target: 80% catalog-based)
Requisition-to-PO cycle time for hydraulic components (monitor for process friction)
risks: Plant resistance due to perceived loss of purchasing flexibility and longer lead times if contracted suppliers cannot match maverick supplier delivery speed
Production disruption risk if contracted suppliers lack capacity or technical capability for specialty hydraulic components currently sourced off-contract
Multi-ERP implementation complexity may delay system control deployment and create compliance gaps between systems
Contracted supplier price increases during contract expansion negotiations may erode savings potential
User workarounds and shadow IT procurement (credit cards, expense reimbursements) may shift rather than eliminate maverick spend
Insufficient contracted supplier coverage for MRO or emergency hydraulic components may force exceptions that undermine compliance culture
erp_actions: SAP: Set purchasing organization-level source lists (ME01) for all hydraulic component material masters with contracted suppliers only; enable source list requirement indicator in material master (MRP2 view)
SAP: Create info records (ME11) with contracted pricing for all hydraulic parts and configure automatic PO pricing from contracts (ME31K)
SAP: Implement vendor block for posting (LFA1/LFB1 posting block field) for identified maverick hydraulic suppliers not meeting quality or compliance standards
SAP: Configure release strategy (ME28) requiring Procurement Manager approval for hydraulic component PRs/POs exceeding $5,000 to non-source-list vendors
Oracle EBS: Update approved supplier lists (ASL) in Purchasing module to restrict hydraulic category requisitions to contracted vendors only
Oracle EBS: Create blanket purchase agreements for contracted hydraulic suppliers and set as preferred on requisition templates
Dynamics 365: Configure procurement category policies to enforce approved vendor lists for hydraulic components category code
Dynamics 365: Set up purchase agreement references and enable automatic agreement pricing for hydraulic requisitions
NetSuite: Create vendor records with preferred vendor flag for contracted suppliers; configure approval routing rules for non-preferred vendor purchases >$5,000
NetSuite: Build saved searches/alerts for hydraulic component purchases to non-contracted vendors for real-time compliance monitoring
Coupa: Load contracted supplier catalogs with punch-out or hosted catalogs for hydraulic components; set as preferred content
Coupa: Configure policy rules to block or route for approval any hydraulic component requisition to non-contracted suppliers
All ERPs: Update payment terms to Net 60 for non-contracted hydraulic suppliers while maintaining Net 30-45 for contracted suppliers to create economic incentive for compliance
All ERPs: Add custom field to PO header tracking contract reference number; make mandatory for hydraulic component purchases
